function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! Here’s a quick guide to help you find the perfect place to order a cake from—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or just want it delivered right to your door.

---

### 1️⃣ Local Bakeries & Specialty Shops  
These places often have unique flavors, custom designs, and great local support.

| Type | What to Look For | Why It Matters |
|------|------------------|----------------|
| **Independent Bakery** | Hand‑crafted cakes, seasonal ingredients | Supports small businesses; often fresher, artisanal quality |
| **Specialty Cake Shop** | Custom décor, themed cakes (e.g., wedding, birthday) | Professional decorators, wide design options |
| **Health‑Focused Bakery** | Gluten‑free, vegan, low‑sugar options | Great for dietary restrictions or health‑conscious friends |

*Tip:* Check their Instagram or Facebook page first—many bakeries post photos of recent creations and customer reviews there.

---

### 2️⃣ Online Delivery Platforms  
If you want convenience and a variety of choices all in one place:

| Platform | How It Works | Pros | Cons |
|----------|--------------|------|------|
| **Uber Eats / DoorDash / Grubhub** | Order through app → driver delivers | Huge selection, real‑time tracking | Delivery fees + tip required |
| **Instacart** | Grocery pickup/delivery → add cake to cart | Same‑day delivery, no extra fee for some items | Limited cake selection compared to dedicated bakeries |
| **Amazon Fresh** | Add cake to grocery list → same‑day delivery | Fast delivery, easy returns | Only available in select cities |

*Pro Tip:* Many platforms let you filter by “cake” or “dessert” and show ratings directly in the app.

---

### 3️⃣ Big‑Box Stores & Supermarkets  
Convenient if you’re already shopping nearby.

| Store | What to Find | Why It’s Handy |
|-------|--------------|----------------|
| **Whole Foods** | Organic, high‑quality ingredients | Often has a bakery section with fresh cakes |
| **Walmart** | Pre‑made cakes, sometimes custom orders | Low cost, easy pickup or delivery |
| **Target** | Seasonal cake kits, pre‑baked options | Quick pick‑up, sometimes free shipping |

*Quick Tip:* Call ahead to confirm they accept custom orders and what their delivery policy is.

---

### 4️⃣ Specialty Online Retailers  
For gourmet or niche cakes (e.g., artisan chocolate, international flavors).

| Site | Specialty | Example Products |
|------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Goldbelly** | Classic American & regional specialties | New York cheesecake, Southern pecan pie |
| **Etsy** | Handmade, custom designs | Personalized wedding cakes, themed cupcakes |
| **The Cake Concierge** | Luxury custom cakes | Wedding cakes with intricate sugar flowers |

*Why Go There?* You’ll get a curated selection and often direct communication with the baker.

---

### 5️⃣ Tips for Ordering

| Question | Where to Ask | Why It Helps |
|----------|--------------|--------------|
| **Delivery Time** | Contact the bakery or platform | Avoid last‑minute surprises |
| **Custom Design Options** | Ask about photo uploads or design templates | Ensures the cake looks exactly how you envision |
| **Dietary Restrictions** | Specify gluten‑free, vegan, nut‑free, etc. | Guarantees everyone can enjoy it |
| **Price Range** | Clarify upfront | Prevents hidden costs (delivery, service fees) |
| **Reviews & Photos** | Read past customer feedback | Gives confidence in quality & reliability |

---

#### Quick Checklist Before Placing Your Order

1. **Decide on the occasion** (birthday, wedding, corporate event).  
2. **Set a budget** (including delivery fees).  
3. **Choose a flavor & size** based on guest count.  
4. **Confirm delivery window** (especially important for events).  
5. **Ask about cancellation policies** (just in case plans change).

---

### 📞 Sample Contacts

| Place | Phone | Website |
|-------|-------|---------|
| **Local Bakery – Sweet Treats** | (555) 123‑4567 | sweettreats.com |
| **Online Delivery – DoorDash** | N/A (app only) | doordash.com |
| **Big‑Box – Walmart** | (555) 987‑6543 | walmart.com |

*(Numbers are placeholders—replace them with actual local contacts.)*

---
